full_judgment:
5. The learned Munsif found that the plaintiffs having paid the advalorem court fees as per Courts Direction in the plaintiff’s prayer "for declaration that the recording of 7/9th share in the disputed tank in RS. Plot No. 8746 is wrong and also for declaration that in spite of that wrong recording the plaintiff's right and interest has not been affected" the suit for declaration of title and confirmation of possession and, as such, the suit as framed was maintainable. The learned Munsif further found that Maghi Chitta is a document of title, that Gul Banu and Bhagyabati were the predecessors of the plaintiffs 41-56, that the defendants suggestion that Md. Waresh Ali, the predecessor of defendants 23-29, 33-35 and 37-40, was the son of Bhagyabati was disproved by CS Khatian Exhibit 1(f) and a and that the descendants of Chasa Md. Waresh Ali got their names recorded with their masters' descendants. He also found that the recording of the 7/9th share in the names of the defendants' predecessors during the RS. Operation was wrong and the plaintiffs are entitled to get a declaration to that effect and that the suit having been filed within 6 years from 15-5-74 on which date defendants threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession on the basis of wrong entry in the RS Khatian, the suit was not barred by limitation or adverse possession. Accordingly the learned Munsif decreed the suit in part declaring that the recording of RS Khatian, Exhibit A (1) and A (2) to the extent of 7/9th share in the names of the defendants' predecessors was wrong and that the right of the plaintiffs and proforma defendants Nos. 41 to 56 to the extent of 16 annas share in the disputed tank has not been affected by RS. Khatians in dispute and further declaring that the plaintiffs and the proforma defendants joint possession with defendants who had purchased 4 gandas of land out of the disputed tank appertaining to RS Plot No. 8746 from the plaintiff No 1 be confirmed. Against the judgment and decree of the learned Munsif the contesting defendants 2 and 8 prepared the appeal and the plaintiffs-respondents in the appeal filed cross-objection for cost of suit. On consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, the learned Sub-ordinate Judge found that in the plaint there is no clear mention of declaration of title in the disputed property, that two negative prayers in prayer (kha) make it affirmative i.e. it tantamount to the position that the principal defendants have got right to disturb in the possession of the entire disputed tank of schedules 1-2 of the plaint, that from the prayer portion of the plaint it appears that schedule 1 property is disputed i.e. 7/9 th share and schedule 2 i.e. 2/9th share is not disputed and thus it creates contradiction in the prayer (kha) and that the negative specific relief of permanent injunction in prayer (ga) is a vague term. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge further found that the recording of RS Khatian in the names of principal defendants is correct, that the principal defendants have possession in the disputed tank, that the Maghi Chitta cannot alone create title in favour or the plaintiffs for the disputed tank and that the plaintiffs side having not rectified the recording of the RS Khatian by filing any suit/case the question of limitation for challenging the RS Khatian also arises, that the plaintiffs and the proforma defendants have joint possession in the disputed tank along with the principal defendants, that the RS Khatian cannot be rectified as the plaintiffs did not take to correct it within the period of limitation, that in the absence of direct evidence the presumption of RS Khatian cannot be rebutted that there is no clear claim by the plaintiff's side that they have title in the entire disputed tank, that the suit is not maintainable and it is barred by limitation. Accordingly he allowed the appeal and rejected the cross-objection and dismissed the suit in reversal of the judgment and decree of the learned Munsif. Against the judgment and decree of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge the plaintiffs have obtained the present Rule. 

 11. In support of the finding of the Sub-ordinate Judge that the Maghi chitta does not create title, Mr. SC Das, the learned Advocate for the opposite-parties 1-2 refers the case of Fazlur Rahim vs Nabendra Krishna Roy and others 17 CWN 151 and the case of Prodyot Kumar Sen Gupta vs Nagendra Kumar Chowdhury, 52 CWN 72. In 17 CWN 151 it was held that a chitta prepared by the Government when interested as a proprietor of the estate concerned could not be said to be a public document and that no special presumption attached to these chittas. In 52 CWN 72 it was held:-It is not necessary for us to hold that Maghi Chitta is wrong. Each record must be presumed to be correct at its date, and since the position indicated by the entries in the chittas could, during the interval, well change into the position indicated by the cadastral and revisional survey records, the latter position is not shown to be impossible or invalid in law, as the learned Sub-ordinate Judge erroneously supposed." In the light of the above cases reported in 17 CWN 151 and 52 CWN 72 it can safely be held that Maghi chitta did not create title in favour of the plaintiff in the disputed tank as has been correctly found by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and the latter position indicated by the RS record is valid in law. As to the presumption of RS khatian and its rebuttal the learned Advocate for the opposite-parties 1-2, has referred to the case of Akrab Ali vs Zahiruddin Kari, 30 DLR (AD) 81 and the case of Meherjan Bibi vs Naimuddin Dhali being dead Raisuddin and others 33 DLR 127 in the case reported in 30 DLR (AD) 81 it is held that according to section 103B(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act every entry in a record of right finally published shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved to be incorrect. In 33 DLR 126 it is held that the presumption of correction as available on the strength of section 103 B (5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, has got to be rebutted by the person who alleges it. In the light of the proposition of law enunciated in the Appellate Division case reported in 30 DLR (AD) 81 the RS Khatian in the present case raises a presumption of its correctness until proved to be incorrect and in view of the decisions in 33 DLR 126 the onus is on the plaintiffs to rebut the presumption of the correctness of the RS khatian in the present case in as, much as, the plaintiffs have alleged that the entry of the RS khatian is wrong. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge has correctly found that there is no direct evidence in the case to rebut presumption of the RS khatian. As such the correctness of the entry of the RS Khatian is not rebutted in the present case.
